main_text.p: Suavis apis cursu Is, nam currit ut optima fingat

l.i: Perge ita: sic clarus rutilis evadere squamis
Mox poteris, gravidas ut Maro laudat apes.

main_text.p:
εἰς φιλίας πεχμήςλον P.
Joh. Conradus Heideggerus,
S. Theolog. Cand.
main_text.head: III.
MARS PHILOSOPHICUS.
main_text.p:
Terras jam dudum ferro populatur & igni
Bellipotens Mavors, cristata cassride cinctus;
Quaque patet tellus vitreo circumsona Ponto
Classica saeva tonant, Taratantara dira cientur,
Horridus exigitur per viscera saucia mucro,
Luctus ubique, nigrae & quam plurima mortis imago est.
Gradivus tremulum vaecors sic concutit orbem.
Haud multum pugna est Bellonā mitior istā,
Ad quam conclamat lituisque tubāque crepante
Effrons turba Sophūm, cui mens & cornea fibra est,
Haud equidem heic fuso pinguescunt sanguine campi;
Haud Martis pulli portant in bella bipennes,
Loricam haud miles ventri succingit atrocem,
Haudque Thraso creperus sua spicula lucida tergit
Arvinā pingui, nec manant stagna cruore.
Alter in alterius sed rumpit nomen habenis
Laxatis mordax, non hospes ab hospite tutus.
Figere discipulus Doctori tentat ocellum,
Et placita inflectit tyro veneranda Magistri.
Indus, Arabs, Syrus, ac Theuton, recutitus apella
Hoc pallent morbo, hac sudant praecordia culpā.

page.notes: The Greek line in the dedication is printed in a small italic hand and is transcribed as legibly as possible; the final lines of the poem are partly obscured by show-through, so some letters, notably in "Sophūm" and "recutitus", may be doubtful. Lines of the poem are printed as verse lines and are given as continuous text within one paragraph for the stanza.
